# Model and source

de Pillis et al. (2025) analysed SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibody (NAb)
activity after a two-dose mRNA COVID-19 primary series in COVID-19-naive and
convalesced adults with two models, both packaged here:

* `dePillis_2025_covid19Vaccine` -- the nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) model.
  Its structural part is the two-state ODE model of NAb dynamics from
  de Pillis et al. (2023, J Theor Biol), fitted in Monolix to the whole NAb
  course from the first dose to the first booster or breakthrough infection.
* `dePillis_2025_covid19Vaccine_lme` -- the linear mixed-effects (LME) model of
  the decay region only (day 37 onward): a cubic polynomial in time on the
  logit NAb scale.

```{r model-load}
nlme <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("dePillis_2025_covid19Vaccine"))
lme <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("dePillis_2025_covid19Vaccine_lme"))
```

* Citation: `r nlme$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-18673-9>
* Correction (author name only, no model content): <https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-26404-3>
* Data and Monolix project deposited by the authors: <https://github.com/depillis/Covid_AntibodyResponse_Analysis>

# Population

The analysis used 324 NAb measurements from 92 adults in the Aditxt
prospective cohort (NCT05379478), sampled November 2020 to April 2022: 68
COVID-19-naive subjects (244 observations) and 24 convalesced subjects, that
is, subjects with COVID-19 before their first vaccine dose (80 observations;
mean 110.7 days from symptom onset to the first dose). Every subject received a
two-dose mRNA primary series: mRNA-1273 (Moderna; 27 naive, 14 convalesced) or
BNT162b2 (Pfizer-BioNTech; 41 naive, 10 convalesced). Mean age was 53.6 years
(naive) and 53.7 years (convalesced); 52.9% of naive and 33.3% of convalesced
subjects were female. Observations after a booster dose or a breakthrough
infection were excluded (Table 1 and Methods of de Pillis 2025).

NAb activity is the percent neutralization of the AditxtScore flow-cytometry
assay, carried in the models as a 0-1 fraction.

```{r population}
str(nlme$population)
```

# Source trace

Values for the NLME model come from Table 3 and Equations 5-8; values for the
LME model come from Table 2 and Equations 3-4. The two Michaelis-Menten
constants of the vaccine compartment are described in the paper as fixed for
the whole population but are not printed; their values (10 and 50) are taken
from the Monolix structural model the authors deposited with the paper.

| Model | Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|-------|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| NLME | `d/dt(antibody) = r1 V + r2 A V + A (r3 - r4 A)` | -- | Eq. 5 |
| NLME | `d/dt(depot_antigen) = u(t) - k1 V / (k2 + V)`, `V(0) = 0` | -- | Eq. 6; dose as a 1-day unit pulse per the deposited model (`Tk0 = 1`, `p = 1`) |
| NLME | `vmax` (k1) | 10 mL/day (fixed) | Deposited `4ParamModel.txt` |
| NLME | `km` (k2) | 50 mL (fixed) | Deposited `4ParamModel.txt` |
| NLME | `r1`, `r2`, `r3`, `r4` typical (naive, mRNA-1273) | 0.089, 0.028, 0.002, 0.010 | Table 3 r10, r20, r30, r40 |
| NLME | A0 typical (naive) | 0.00003 | Table 3 A00 |
| NLME | Convalesced effects on logit r1, r2, r3, r4, A0 | -3.670, -5.860, -1.440, -2.100, 16.500 | Table 3 beta11, beta21, beta31, beta41, beta01 |
| NLME | BNT162b2 effects on logit r1, r2, r3 | -0.905, 1.760, -0.862 | Table 3 beta12, beta22, beta32 |
| NLME | IIV SD on logit r1, r2, r3, r4, A0 | 0.345, 0.611, 0.323, 0.675, 3.630 | Table 3 omega1-omega4, omega0 |
| NLME | Correlations r2-r1, r3-r1, r4-r1, r3-r2, r4-r2, r4-r3 | -0.260, 0.662, -0.145, 0.151, 0.841, 0.346 | Table 3 |
| NLME | Residual error `a`, `b` (combined1, logit scale) | 0.348, 0.206 | Table 3; Eq. 7 |
| NLME | Logit bounds m, M | -0.00954434, 1.01970 | Results text after Eq. 7 |
| LME | `logit(y) = beta0 + beta1 tc + beta2 tc^2 + beta3 tc^3`, `tc = (t - 178)/365` | -- | Eqs. 3-4; tbar approx 178 days in Results |
| LME | beta00, beta01, beta10, beta20, beta21, beta30 | -0.082, 1.535, -4.015, 5.711, 4.890, -5.715 | Table 2 |
| LME | SD of random intercept and slope; correlation | 1.032, 2.103; -0.420 | Table 2 |
| LME | Residual SD on the logit scale | 0.327 | Table 2 |

Table 3 and Table 2 label each row with a symbol only; the mapping of the
first covariate coefficient (`beta_k1`) to convalesced status and the second
(`beta_k2`) to the BNT162b2 vaccine follows Eq. 8, and is confirmed below by
reproducing the per-group medians of Figure 3.

# NLME model: typical NAb courses

Doses enter `depot_antigen` as `amt = 1` infused over 1 day. The second dose is
given on day 21 for BNT162b2 and day 28 for mRNA-1273, the labelled schedules.

```{r nlme-events}
make_events <- function(ids, seropos, tozinameran, obs_times) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(ids), function(i) {
    t2 <- if (tozinameran[i] == 1) 21 else 28
    doses <- data.frame(
      id = ids[i], time = c(0, t2), amt = 1, rate = 1, evid = 1,
      cmt = "depot_antigen"
    )
    obs <- data.frame(
      id = ids[i], time = obs_times, amt = NA_real_, rate = NA_real_,
      evid = 0, cmt = "antibody"
    )
    out <- bind_rows(doses, obs)
    out$SARS_SEROPOS <- seropos[i]
    out$TRT_TOZINAMERAN <- tozinameran[i]
    out
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

# Typical-value solve. With all random effects zeroed, rxode2 warns that a
# multi-subject simulation has no omega; that is the intent here.
solve_typical <- function(model, events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(model), events, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}

groups <- expand.grid(SARS_SEROPOS = 0:1, TRT_TOZINAMERAN = 0:1)
groups$id <- seq_len(nrow(groups))
groups$label <- paste(
  ifelse(groups$SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive"),
  ifelse(groups$TRT_TOZINAMERAN == 1, "BNT162b2", "mRNA-1273"),
  sep = ", "
)
ev_typ <- make_events(groups$id, groups$SARS_SEROPOS, groups$TRT_TOZINAMERAN, seq(0, 455, by = 1))
typ <- solve_typical(nlme, ev_typ) |>
  left_join(groups[, c("id", "label")], by = "id")
```

```{r nlme-typical-plot}
ggplot(typ, aes(time, nab, colour = label)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since first dose", y = "NAb activity (fraction neutralization)",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical NLME NAb courses by convalesced status and vaccine"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The typical naive subject starts near zero, rises after each dose and peaks a
few weeks after the second dose; the typical convalesced subject starts near
full neutralization and decays more slowly, the paper's main conclusion.

```{r nlme-typical-check}
typ_summary <- typ |>
  group_by(label) |>
  summarise(
    nab_day0 = nab[time == 0],
    peak = max(nab),
    tpeak = time[which.max(nab)],
    nab_day365 = nab[time == 365],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(typ_summary, digits = 3)

naive_mod <- typ_summary[typ_summary$label == "Naive, mRNA-1273", ]
conv_mod <- typ_summary[typ_summary$label == "Convalesced, mRNA-1273", ]
stopifnot(
  # Naive start equals the typical A0 of 0.00003 (Table 3).
  abs(naive_mod$nab_day0 - 0.00003) < 1e-6,
  # Convalesced start equals expit(logit(0.00003) + 16.5) (Table 3).
  abs(conv_mod$nab_day0 - plogis(qlogis(0.00003) + 16.5)) < 1e-6,
  # Naive peak comes after the second dose, within 3 weeks of it.
  naive_mod$tpeak > 28, naive_mod$tpeak < 49,
  # Convalesced NAb stays above naive at one year (Results, Fig. 5).
  conv_mod$nab_day365 > naive_mod$nab_day365
)
```

# NLME model: individual parameters (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows boxplots of the logit of the empirical-Bayes individual
parameters by convalesced status. Each group mixes the two vaccines (Table 1),
so the model's group median of a logit parameter is the median of a two-
component normal mixture: the typical logit value for each vaccine, weighted by
the Table 1 split, with the Table 3 IIV SD. That median is computed exactly
below and compared with the Figure 3 medians, which were read from the figure
by the maintainers. A simulated cohort is plotted alongside for illustration.

```{r fig3-cohort}
set.seed(20251006)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251006)
n_per_arm <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_per_arm),
  SARS_SEROPOS = rep(0:1, each = n_per_arm)
)
# Table 1: naive 27 mRNA-1273 / 41 BNT162b2; convalesced 14 / 10.
cohort$TRT_TOZINAMERAN <- c(
  rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 41 / 68),
  rbinom(n_per_arm, 1, 10 / 24)
)
obs_grid <- c(0, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28, 35, 42, 60, 90, 120, 160, 200, 250, 300, 365, 455)
ev_coh <- make_events(cohort$id, cohort$SARS_SEROPOS, cohort$TRT_TOZINAMERAN, obs_grid)
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(nlme, ev_coh, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  left_join(cohort, by = c("id", "SARS_SEROPOS", "TRT_TOZINAMERAN"))
```

```{r fig3-compare}
indiv <- sim |>
  distinct(id, SARS_SEROPOS, r1, r2, r3, r4, nab0) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive")) |>
  pivot_longer(c(nab0, r1, r2, r3, r4), names_to = "parameter", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(logit_value = qlogis(value))

fig3_ref <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("Naive", "Convalesced"), each = 5),
  parameter = rep(c("nab0", "r1", "r2", "r3", "r4"), 2),
  fig3_median = c(-10.5, -2.9, -2.3, -7.0, -4.6, 7.0, -6.3, -8.7, -8.2, -6.65)
)

th <- nlme$theta
iiv_sd <- sqrt(diag(nlme$omega))
typical_logit <- function(parameter, seropos, tozinameran) {
  base <- th[[paste0("logit", parameter)]]
  e_c <- th[[paste0("e_sars_seropos_", parameter)]]
  e_d_name <- paste0("e_trt_tozinameran_", parameter)
  e_d <- if (e_d_name %in% names(th)) th[[e_d_name]] else 0
  base + e_c * seropos + e_d * tozinameran
}
mixture_median <- function(parameter, seropos) {
  w <- if (seropos == 1) 10 / 24 else 41 / 68
  mu0 <- typical_logit(parameter, seropos, 0)
  mu1 <- typical_logit(parameter, seropos, 1)
  s <- iiv_sd[[paste0("etalogit", parameter)]]
  f <- function(m) (1 - w) * pnorm(m, mu0, s) + w * pnorm(m, mu1, s) - 0.5
  uniroot(f, c(-60, 60), tol = 1e-8)$root
}
fig3_cmp <- fig3_ref |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(
    model_median = mixture_median(parameter, as.integer(group == "Convalesced")),
    diff = model_median - fig3_median
  ) |>
  ungroup()

fig3_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "Parameter (logit)" = parameter,
    "Model median" = model_median, "Figure 3 median" = fig3_median,
    "Difference" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

stopifnot(
  # Central agreement across all ten group x parameter medians. A swapped
  # covariate column (convalesced vs vaccine) or a misread coefficient moves
  # a median by 2-6 logit units.
  median(abs(fig3_cmp$diff)) < 0.5,
  # The loosest is convalesced A0 (model 6.1 vs Figure 3 7.0): its
  # coefficient is poorly determined (SE 72.5 on 16.5), so the empirical-Bayes
  # estimates in Figure 3 lean toward the data rather than the typical value.
  max(abs(fig3_cmp$diff)) < 1.5
)
```

```{r fig3-plot}
ggplot(indiv, aes(factor(group, c("Naive", "Convalesced")), logit_value)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "grey80", outlier.size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(
    data = fig3_ref, aes(group, fig3_median),
    colour = "red", shape = 4, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "logit(parameter)",
    title = "Replicates Figure 3 of de Pillis 2025",
    caption = "Boxes: simulated individual parameters. Red crosses: Figure 3 medians."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# NLME model: simulated NAb distribution against the observations

The authors deposited the NLME analysis dataset with the paper. Its observed
NAb distribution by convalesced status and time bin (summarised by the
maintainers and hard-coded below; the deposited dataset holds 100 subjects,
slightly more than the 92 analysed in the article) is compared with simulated
observations including residual error. Bins with fewer than 10 observations are
shown but not used in the check.

The structural model does not bound NAb activity at 1: in subjects with large
r1 and r2 the vaccine-driven terms push A above full neutralization for a few
weeks after the second dose. The logit residual model is undefined above the
upper bound M = 1.0197, so those simulated observations are returned as `NaN`.
They are set to 1 (the assay ceiling) before summarising.

```{r above-bound}
above <- sim |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    pct_rows_above_M = 100 * mean(nab > 1.01970),
    pct_subjects_ever_above_M = 100 * mean(tapply(nab > 1.01970, id, any)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(above, digits = 1)
sim <- sim |> mutate(sim = ifelse(is.na(sim) & nab > 1.01970, 1, sim))
stopifnot(!anyNA(sim$sim))
```

```{r vpc}
obs_ref <- data.frame(
  group = rep(c("Naive", "Convalesced"), each = 7),
  bin = rep(c("[0,10)", "[10,30)", "[30,60)", "[60,120)", "[120,200)", "[200,300)", "[300,500)"), 2),
  n_obs = c(11, 32, 35, 42, 39, 59, 26, 6, 14, 14, 15, 10, 12, 7),
  obs_q10 = c(0.038, 0.150, 0.310, 0.393, 0.223, 0.208, 0.080, 0.538, 0.414, 0.921, 0.800, 0.588, 0.345, 0.286),
  obs_median = c(0.142, 0.375, 0.870, 0.689, 0.470, 0.350, 0.235, 0.985, 0.990, 0.975, 0.920, 0.787, 0.728, 0.499),
  obs_q90 = c(0.170, 0.892, 0.981, 0.934, 0.764, 0.587, 0.452, 0.996, 0.996, 0.995, 0.992, 0.947, 0.901, 0.921)
)

sim_bins <- sim |>
  mutate(
    group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive"),
    bin = as.character(cut(time, c(0, 10, 30, 60, 120, 200, 300, 500), right = FALSE))
  ) |>
  group_by(group, bin) |>
  summarise(
    sim_q10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), sim_median = median(sim), sim_q90 = quantile(sim, 0.9),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
vpc_cmp <- left_join(obs_ref, sim_bins, by = c("group", "bin"))

vpc_cmp |>
  dplyr::select(group, bin, n_obs, obs_median, sim_median, obs_q10, sim_q10, obs_q90, sim_q90) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "Days" = bin, "N obs" = n_obs,
    "Obs median" = obs_median, "Sim median" = sim_median,
    "Obs P10" = obs_q10, "Sim P10" = sim_q10,
    "Obs P90" = obs_q90, "Sim P90" = sim_q90
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

vpc_gate <- vpc_cmp |> filter(n_obs >= 10)
stopifnot(
  median(abs(vpc_gate$sim_median - vpc_gate$obs_median)) < 0.1,
  quantile(abs(vpc_gate$sim_median - vpc_gate$obs_median), 0.9) < 0.25
)
```

```{r vpc-plot}
bin_mid <- c(
  "[0,10)" = 5, "[10,30)" = 20, "[30,60)" = 45, "[60,120)" = 90,
  "[120,200)" = 160, "[200,300)" = 250, "[300,500)" = 375
)
vpc_long <- vpc_cmp |>
  mutate(time = bin_mid[bin], group = factor(group, c("Naive", "Convalesced")))
ggplot(vpc_long, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = sim_q10, ymax = sim_q90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = sim_median), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(aes(y = obs_median, size = n_obs), colour = "black") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = obs_q10, ymax = obs_q90), width = 8) +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since first dose", y = "NAb activity (fraction neutralization)",
    size = "N obs",
    title = "Simulated (blue: median, P10-P90) vs observed (black) NAb by time bin"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# LME model: decay-region mean curves (Figure 2(i))

The LME model applies only from day 37 after the first dose. Its population
curve is the back-transformed fixed-effect polynomial (random effects at zero).

```{r lme-curves}
lme_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(0:1, function(c) {
  data.frame(id = c + 1, time = seq(37, 455, by = 1), evid = 0, SARS_SEROPOS = c)
}))
lme_typ <- solve_typical(lme, lme_ev) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive"))

# Values read from the Figure 2(i) mean curves by the maintainers.
fig2_ref <- data.frame(
  group = c("Naive", "Naive", "Convalesced", "Convalesced", "Convalesced"),
  time = c(37, 455, 37, 280, 455),
  fig2 = c(0.92, 0.07, 0.98, 0.74, 0.88)
)
fig2_cmp <- fig2_ref |>
  left_join(lme_typ[, c("group", "time", "nab")], by = c("group", "time")) |>
  mutate(diff = nab - fig2)
fig2_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "Day" = time, "Figure 2(i)" = fig2,
    "LME model" = nab, "Difference" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(max(abs(fig2_cmp$diff)) < 0.05)
```

```{r lme-plot}
lme_sim_ev <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(2 * n_per_arm), function(i) {
  data.frame(
    id = i, time = seq(37, 455, by = 14), evid = 0,
    SARS_SEROPOS = as.integer(i > n_per_arm)
  )
}))
lme_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(lme, lme_sim_ev, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive")) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(q10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), q90 = quantile(sim, 0.9), .groups = "drop")

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = lme_sim, aes(time, ymin = q10, ymax = q90, fill = group),
    alpha = 0.15
  ) +
  geom_line(data = lme_typ, aes(time, nab, colour = group), linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_ref, aes(time, fig2, colour = group), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Convalesced = "red", Naive = "steelblue")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Convalesced = "red", Naive = "steelblue")) +
  labs(
    x = "Days since first dose", y = "NAb activity (fraction neutralization)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    title = "Replicates Figure 2(i) of de Pillis 2025",
    caption = "Lines: LME population curves. Ribbons: simulated P10-P90. Crosses: values read from Figure 2(i)."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Agreement between the two models in the decay region

Both models were fitted to the same observations, so the NLME typical course
for the cohort should lie close to the LME population curve after day 37. The
NLME median below is over the simulated cohort without residual error.

```{r cross-model}
nlme_med <- sim |>
  filter(time >= 60) |>
  mutate(group = ifelse(SARS_SEROPOS == 1, "Convalesced", "Naive")) |>
  group_by(group, time) |>
  summarise(nlme_median = median(nab), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(lme_typ[, c("group", "time", "nab")], by = c("group", "time")) |>
  dplyr::rename(lme_population = nab)
knitr::kable(nlme_med, digits = 3)
stopifnot(median(abs(nlme_med$nlme_median - nlme_med$lme_population)) < 0.15)
```

# Non-compartmental analysis

Not applicable. Neither model describes a drug concentration; the output is a
bounded (0-1) antibody activity driven by unit vaccine pulses, so NCA
parameters such as Cmax or AUC have no published counterpart. Validation
instead uses the reported individual-parameter distributions (Figure 3), the
LME mean curves (Figure 2(i)), the deposited observations and the agreement
between the two models.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Fixed vaccine-cell kinetics.** The paper states that k1 and k2 are fixed
  for the whole population without printing them. The values `vmax = 10`
  mL/day and `km = 50` mL are taken from the authors' deposited Monolix
  structural model, which says they align with the earlier de Pillis 2023 model.
* **Vaccine dose.** The paper describes u(t) as a unit pulse on each vaccination
  day. The deposited Monolix model implements it as an amount of 1 delivered
  zero-order over 1 day into V, reproduced here with `amt = 1, rate = 1`.
  V(0) = 0.
* **Second-dose timing.** Not stated in the paper. The vignette uses the labelled
  schedules, day 21 (BNT162b2) and day 28 (mRNA-1273); the deposited data have
  median second-dose days of 21 and 29.
* **Logit-normal residual error.** Eq. 7 applies Monolix's combined1 error
  `a + b * f` to the logit-transformed prediction with bounds m and M. This is
  encoded with `add() + propT() + combined1() + logitNorm(NA, m, M)`, where
  `propT()` scales with the transformed prediction. Monolix computed the upper
  bound as 1.01970 (Results); the deposited project file prints 1.01979, and
  the paper's value is used.
* **Predictions above full neutralization.** Eq. 5 has no term that holds A
  below 1, and the logistic carrying capacity r3/r4 only pulls A back after
  the vaccine pulse has cleared. For simulated subjects drawn from the IIV
  distribution, A can briefly exceed the upper logit bound M; their simulated
  observations are undefined there and are set to the assay ceiling of 1 in
  this vignette. Users simulating observations should do the same.
* **Deposited Monolix estimates differ from Table 3.** The deposited project's
  exported population parameters come from a later run (for example
  `r1_pop` 0.0954 and correlation r3-r1 -0.109 against 0.089 and 0.662 in
  Table 3). The published Table 3 estimates are used throughout.
* **LME centring.** Results gives tbar as approximately 178 days; the deposited
  decay-region data give 178.04 days. The rounded published value is used.
* **LME vaccine-type and sex models.** The paper also fitted LME variants with
  vaccine type (Eq. 9, Figure 2(ii)-(iii)) and sex; their coefficients are not
  reported, so only the convalesced-status model (Eqs. 3-4, Table 2) is
  packaged.
* **Observation variable.** Both models name the output `nab` (NAb activity as a
  0-1 fraction), which is not a registered observation name, so
  `checkModelConventions()` reports it as non-canonical.
* **Covariates.** The paper's convalesced indicator C is carried as
  `SARS_SEROPOS`. Subjects were vaccine-naive at baseline and naive subjects with
  nucleocapsid antibodies before vaccination were excluded, so within this
  population convalesced status coincides with baseline seropositivity from
  prior infection. The paper's Pfizer indicator D is `TRT_TOZINAMERAN`
  (reference mRNA-1273).
